2029 Estuary Works handover memorandum. This is a fictional document QA fixture.
The Works Board uses spring inspections to transfer responsibility across three crews. Each station has a working log, a field action, and a signed release order. The field log describes conditions observed by the first crew. The release order overrides earlier notes only when it explicitly says 'controlling copy'. Tool codes are listed for audit and may refer to a physical location that remained closed. Do not infer that a location reopened solely because the crew finished sampling. The question concerns the controlling Harbor Nine order, and the rest of this document is included so a reader must distinguish it from earlier drafts and the procedures of adjacent stations.

Station 01, Alder Gate. Inspection date April 8.
On arrival the crew requested temporary access through the west pedestrian portal. The gate operations logged 7 routine samples and compared two parallel readings with the handheld instrument. Each observer filed one copy of the route sketch. The original went into the station file and the annotated copy went to the duty desk. During the afternoon the crew isolated the lowest test point, checked that the relief path remained open, and reinstalled the barrier after the second reading. A passing sample was a procedural prerequisite. It did not by itself grant a general release. A duty officer had to mark the route release ledger and send a confirmation with the station name, route and shift explicitly recorded.
The delivery register for Alder Gate lists replacement hardware and the corresponding handover witnesses. Spare fittings remained sealed pending the following inventory check. The photographs were archived with the morning and evening surveys in separate envelopes. Any note containing an unapproved shorthand for the west pedestrian portal was retained as a draft, with a cross-reference to the signed entry. The team kept one observer at the service boundary until an authorized worker took over. Nearby stations used their own release rules. An instruction in this subsection did not apply across the whole estuary.
